actions: Read-only review of diff, callers, tests, existing Key state logic and generated pure key-name mapping. No production/helper edits, builds, ADB or device action. Only this review JSON written.
scope_note: app/build.gradle.kts was also modified during root-owned build preparation. Its contents are outside this two-file production review; no changes were made by reviewer.
conclusion: The patch correctly turns unparseable drawable values into null, allowing existing caller fallback, while retaining valid transparent colors including integer zero and the existing image/custom-alias resolution. It does not change Key classification, text-color policy, fallback chain priority or scheme generation. Android runtime behavior remains to be established by the root-run probe; no device pass is claimed.

confirmed_behavior.before: ColorManager.parseDrawable caught the parse exception, used Color.TRANSPARENT and returned non-null GradientDrawable.
confirmed_behavior.after: ColorTable.parseValue yields Value.None; parseDrawable returns null, so Key.getDrawable can take its existing Elvis fallback.
confirmed_behavior.review: Correct intended behavioral change. A canonical key whose table entry is None also tries literal spelling and now returns null instead of a transparent placeholder.

confirmed_behavior.case: Valid color integer zero / explicit transparent
confirmed_behavior.mechanism: parseColor(value)?.let { Value.Color(it) } tests nullability, not numeric truthiness. Int0 therefore remains Value.Color(0), producing a non-null GradientDrawable.
confirmed_behavior.review: Preserved. This applies to actual Android parser-accepted transparent forms, not arbitrary malformed strings.

confirmed_behavior.mechanism: Actual ColorManager still calls the unchanged ColorUtils.parseColor. Successful Int values are passed unchanged to GradientDrawable.setColor.
confirmed_behavior.review: Preserved by source; named/zero/hex actual Android rendering is covered by planned device controls, not proven by JVM fake parser.

confirmed_behavior.mechanism: Same lowercase suffix classification and unchanged imageDrawable/path/cache/NinePatch decoding. Table Image entries and custom image values still use the same loading path. Missing file already returned null before the patch.
confirmed_behavior.review: Preserved. Refactoring means injected parseColor is no longer invoked for image strings; current production parser callback is pure and this is not an observable supported-input regression.

confirmed_behavior.case: Custom scheme aliases and theme fallback chains
confirmed_behavior.mechanism: resolveRawSource/resolveRaw are unchanged: explicit nonempty scheme value, then theme fallback hop, then canonical built-in fallback. Cycle and empty-value handling are unchanged.
confirmed_behavior.review: Preserved. Direct valid/transparent values still beat fallback; absent custom aliases now allow caller fallback rather than blocking it with a transparent drawable.

confirmed_behavior.mechanism: The baseline ColorTable already classified a failed parse as Value.None and listed invalidValues. New parseValue centralizes the same classification for table and drawable parsing; invalidValues/unresolvedKeys semantics are preserved.
confirmed_behavior.review: Do not describe this as fixing ColorTable previously converting invalid values to Color(0); the old transparent conversion was in ColorManager.parseDrawable.

confirmed_behavior.mechanism: Reviewed KeyView, themed view background/image assignments, ToolButton and decorDrawable consumers. KeyView explicitly returns when drawable is null; other inspected theme consumers accept nullable backgrounds/drawables.
confirmed_behavior.review: No new null dereference found. Invalid styles can now reveal caller/default/parent backgrounds rather than draw an accidental transparent placeholder; this is intentional and broader than only the two named schemes.

helper_oracle_review.normal_fixture: Real first TextKey from expanded default layout: click q, bh1/th1. q is nonfunctional, nonmodifier and nonsticky.
helper_oracle_review.functional_fixture: The asset declares functional presets but none of its layout keys use them. Helper explicitly copies the real q TextKey, uses real functional Keyboard_letter preset (send Eisu_toggle, nonmodifier/nonsticky), and real bgn/tgn aliases. It reports this construction and does not present it as a declared layout key.

states.background: TextKey.hilitedKeyBackColor if valid, else hilited_key_back_color; real q override is empty
states.text: TextKey.hilitedKeyTextColor if valid, else hilited_key_text_color; real q override is empty

states.background: Since bgn is explicitly nonempty, Key uses keyBackground: valid bgn, else generic key_back_color. It does not use off_key_back_color for this fixture.
hilited_off_key_back_color through existing canonical chain, with old hlKeyBackground fallback only if absent

helper_oracle_review.state_reset: onReleased then setOn(false), optional setOn(true), optional onPressed. q and Keyboard_letter are not sticky, so reset does not create an unintended on state. Same two Key objects persist across all scheme changes; parent modifiers remain0.
helper_oracle_review.rendering: Expected color is drawn through ColorDrawable to an 8x8 Canvas before comparing to actual drawable center pixel. This accounts for alpha/premultiplication and is a synthetic swatch, not full KeyView render. Actual text-color Int is compared directly.
helper_oracle_review.bounds: 46 unique schemes, default revisited at end; 282 state observations. Required original symptom rows specifically google_plus/normal and tantsing/normal. Up to400 violation records, 20s main task bound and120s watchdog.
helper_oracle_review.public_API_and_native: Public parsing, ColorManager/ThemeScope, Keyboard and Key APIs only. Key.getLabel/getAction are avoided. Generated key-name mapping is pure when/constant lookup; Eisu_toggle maps to KeyEvent.KEYCODE_EISU. No Rime session or JNI invocation appears in helper path. Application-owned background work is outside this static claim.
limitations: Functional off state with an empty custom background is not one of the 282 real-theme state rows; current Key retains its preexisting offKeyBackground policy.
The key state oracle assumes shipped standard-theme canonical backgrounds resolve to colors; unit all-palette checks and runtime will validate the actual asset.

The helper produces expected baseline assertion failure and passed=false, rather than swallowing it as a passing baseline. The actual test runner must inspect targeted observations and expected_observation_matches, not only shell exit.
Restoration runs in finally for normal failures and records preference readback plus owned PNG deletion. A hard watchdog/process termination can prevent cleanup; root must retain cleanup evidence.

meaningful_coverage: Uses real production ThemeTestSupport decoding (ThemeYaml/DSL) and all46 shipped standard palettes; identifies bh1/th1 omissions and concrete Google+/tantsing generic colors.
Checks explicit key-background overrides versus generic availability across all declared per-key aliases and all palettes, rather than asserting a desired contrast ratio.
Checks nullable value domain separation for valid0, ordinaryhex, invalid values, images, custom fallback chains and direct-value priority.
test_parser_limits: parseHex is a test dependency injected into ColorTable classification, not actual Android ColorUtils/Color.parseColor execution and not an Android Drawable test.
The listed unit fixtures use lowercase hex forms; named colors and framework parsing/Bitmap decode are not proven by these JVM assertions.

parseHex is not a complete drop-in for ColorUtils for every input: for example its ignore-case 0X acceptance can differ from the existing production normalization regex. The patch does not modify ColorUtils, and no uppercase0X compatibility claim should be made.
Image suffix/value classification assertions do not verify actual image decoding, image existence or Android NinePatch behavior.
Actual Android ThemeScope.drawable/ColorManager.getDrawable and Key fallback are the separately planned instrumentation validation. No unit/device test was run by this reviewer.

intentional_behavior_change_and_limits: Malformed color values that previously happened to yield transparency now return null; themes intending transparency must use a parser-accepted explicit transparent color.
No guarantee that all palettes have high contrast, all backgrounds are opaque, or issue2159 historical visual symptoms are fully eliminated.
Key functional classification/fallback strategy, ThemeColors exceptions for non-color canonical entries, image format/suffix support and generation caching are unchanged.
No crash or rendered keyboard outcome is established by this static review. Root must bind original/diagnostic APK identity and runtime controls before claiming device validation.
